title: On Amusing the children with a story
subtitle: 情感心理 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 情感心理（人与自我·做人与做事·情绪与心理）
meta: 主题语境：情感心理（人与自我·做人与做事·情绪与心理）　|　核心词汇：amuse　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 amuse 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1967 the nurse ① amused the children with a story twice over, and every sufferer in the ward said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three nights on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the nurse ② amuses the children with a story year after year without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ amuse the children with a story at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ amused the children with a story before — a line in the report for April 1961 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Amusing the children with a story twice over, the nurse said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the thermometer at the far cupboard, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ amuse the long wait with songs year after year, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Amuse the long wait with songs at once and never mention it again.

By 1974 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the report, and a new sufferer from the next ward ⑧ amuses the long wait with songs twice over every night without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the cupboard, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ amused the children with a story again when nobody else would.

⑩ To amuse the children with a story, my mother said in 1979, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the ward remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the ward forgets, somebody amuses the children with a story year after year again and somebody must amuse the children with a story twice over all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 逗乐（一般过去式 amused the children with a story：1967 年护士头一回这样做，来回两遍）
B. v. 逗乐（一般现在 amuses the children with a story：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 逗乐（不定式 to amuse the children with a story：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 逗乐（过去完成时 had amused the children with a story：1961 年四月的护理记录上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 逗乐（动名词 amusing the children with a story 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 消磨（amuse the long wait with songs：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去消磨用歌声打发那段长等）
G. v. 消磨（amuse the long wait with songs：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 逗乐（后段两处：新来的病患照例 amuses the long wait with songs，而母亲又一次 amused the children with a story）

answers.why: amuse 意为“逗乐”，1967 年护士来回两遍逗乐用一段故事逗孩子们，那是病房里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 amused。
amuse 意为“逗乐”，自那以后护士年年地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 amuses。
amuse 意为“逗乐”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯逗乐用一段故事逗孩子们”，此处为不定式 to amuse the children with a story。
amuse 意为“逗乐”，护理记录里 四月 那行字说明早在 1974 年之前就有人逗乐过，故用过去完成时 had amused。
amuse 意为“逗乐”，护士说“逗乐用一段故事逗孩子们这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 amusing the children with a story 作主语。
amuse 意为“消磨”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去消磨用歌声打发那段长等”，should ever 之后用原形 amuse the long wait with songs。
amuse 意为“消磨”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻消磨用歌声打发那段长等（amuse the long wait with songs at once），以后再也不要提起。
amuse 意为“逗乐”，新来的病患每个夜晚都照例消磨用歌声打发那段长等，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 amuses。
amuse 意为“逗乐”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次来回两遍逗乐用一段故事逗孩子们，用一般过去式 amused 叙述。
amuse 意为“逗乐”，结尾那句是母亲 1979 年的话：要逗乐用一段故事逗孩子们，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和病房记住的那一件。

多年以后，护士仍年年地做着同一件事，不必有人开口。（amuses the children with a story）

早在 1961 年就有人逗乐用一段故事逗孩子们，四月那天护理记录上的一行字就是证据。（had amused the children with a story）
护士说过，来回两遍逗乐用一段故事逗孩子们这件事，是九分耐心一分胆气。（amusing the children with a story 作主语）
老手们留下的规矩说得明白：立刻消磨用歌声打发那段长等，以后再也不要提起。（amuse the long wait with songs，祈使句）

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 amuse 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1967 the nurse amused the children with a story twice over, and nobody in the ward forgot it.
Even now the nurse amuses the children with a story year after year whenever the ward asks.
Amusing the children with a story twice over, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever amuse the long wait with songs year after year, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new sufferer from the next ward amuses the long wait with songs twice over every night, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother amused the children with a story again, and the ward remembered that half.
